 ADVERTISEMENT   Filtered By: Weather Weather Typhoon Rosal slightly intensifies; Wind Signal No. 2 remains over Batanes 
 By LYJAH TIFFANY BONZO, GMA News Published October 23, 2026 5:43pm 
 + Add GMA on Google Make this your preferred source to get more updates from this publisher on Google. Courtesy: PAGASA Tropical Cyclone Wind Signal No. 2 remains hoisted over Batanes as Typhoon Rosal (international name: Champi) slightly intensified, the state weather bureau PAGASA said Friday afternoon. 
 In its 5 p.m. bulletin, the bureau said Rosal has slightly gained strength as it continues to move north-northwestward over the sea east of Taiwan. 
 As of 4 p.m., Typhoon Rosal was spotted 385 kph north-northeast of Itbayat, Batanes, with maximum sustained winds of 155 kph and gusts of up to 190 kph. 
 PAGASA has also raised Wind Signal No. 1 over the following areas:

 Northern portion of Cagayan (Santa Ana, Gonzaga, Lal-Lo, Santa Teresita, Camalaniugan, Aparri, Buguey, Gattaran, Baggao, Santa Praxedes, Claveria, Sanchez-Mira, Pamplona, Ballesteros, Abulug, Allacapan, Lasam)
 Babuyan Islands
 Northern portion of Ilocos Norte (Pagudpud, Adams, Bangui, Vintar, Burgos, Bacarra, Pasuquin, Carasi, Dumalneg) 
 Northern portion of Apayao (Calanasan, Luna, Santa Marcela, Flora, Pudtol)
 According to the weather bureau, the periphery of Rosal is expected to bring strong to gale-force winds over most of Luzon and Visayas, Zamboanga Peninsula, Misamis Occidental, Basilan, Tawi-Tawi, Davao Occidental, and Davao Oriental.
 Rosal is forecast to exit the Philippine Area of Responsibility on Saturday morning. 
 "ROSAL is expected to steady weaken within the forecast period. It may be downgraded into a severe tropical storm by Sunday morning," PAGASA added. 
 The state weather bureau advised the public and concerned disaster risk reduction and management offices to take all necessary measures to protect life and property. — VDV, GMA News
